text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The decrease in first ionization enthalpy from B to Al is much larger than that from Al to Ga.

Statement II : The d orbitals in Ga are completely filled.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both the statements I and II are correct
Both the statements I and II are incorrect
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is correct as the decrease in first ionization enthalpy from B to Al is indeed much larger than from Al to Ga. This is due to the shielding effect of the electron in the outermost shell and the increased effective nuclear charge as one moves from B to Al and from Al to Ga.

Statement II is also correct, as the d orbitals in Ga are indeed completely filled. This results in the shielding effect being maximum for Ga and thus, the decrease in first ionization enthalpy from Al to Ga is smaller compared to that from B to Al.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: When a hydrocarbon A undergoes combustion in the presence of air, it requires 9.5 equivalents of oxygen and produces 3 equivalents of water. What is the molecular formula of A?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{x}H_{y}+\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )O_{2}\to xCO_{2}+\frac{y}{2}H_{2}O$

$\frac{y}{2}=3$

$y=6$

$x+\frac{y}{4}=\frac{19}{2}$

$x=\frac{19}{2}-\frac{3}{2}=8$

So, formula is $C_{8}H_{6}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
The set of correct statements is :

(i) Manganese exhibits +7 oxidation state in its oxide.

(ii) Ruthenium and Osmium exhibit +8 oxidation state in their oxides.

(iii) Sc shows +4 oxidation state which is oxidizing in nature.

(iv) Cr shows oxidising nature in +6 oxidation state.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(i) In $\mathrm{Mn}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$ manganese is in the +7 oxidation state, so (i) is correct.

(ii) Ruthenium and osmium form the tetroxides $\mathrm{RuO}{}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{OsO}{}_{4}$, in which they are in the +8 state, so (ii) is correct.

(iii) Sc ($3d^{1}4s^{2}$) shows only the +3 state, which gives the stable noble-gas configuration $[\text{Ar}]$; a +4 state would need removal of an electron from this core, so (iii) is incorrect.

(iv) Cr(VI), as in $\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}{}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$, is readily reduced to Cr(III), so chromium is oxidising in the +6 state and (iv) is correct.

The correct statements are (i), (ii) and (iv).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Correct order of spin only magnetic moment of the following complex ions is :

(Given At.no. Fe : 26, Co : 27)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$; weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ gives high spin $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ with 5 unpaired electrons, $μ=\sqrt{35}=5.92\text{BM}$.

$[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$; $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ gives high spin $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ with 4 unpaired electrons, $μ=\sqrt{24}=4.90\text{BM}$.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$: for the highly charged $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ion, oxalate splits the d orbitals by more than the pairing energy, so the complex is low spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ ($d^{2}sp^{3}$) and diamagnetic, $μ=0$; $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is the usual exception that gives high-spin $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$.

The order is $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}>[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}>[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The one giving maximum number of isomeric alkenes on dehydrohalogenation reaction is (excluding rearrangement)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dehydrohalogenation removes Br together with a hydrogen from a β-carbon, so the number of alkenes depends on which β-carbons carry H and on whether the alkenes show geometrical isomerism.

(A) $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: the β-carbon C-3 is quaternary, so only C-1 can lose H, giving 3,3-dimethylpent-1-ene only (1 alkene).

(B) $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: both β-carbons are equivalent, giving propene only (1 alkene).

(C) $\mathrm{BrCH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: the only β-carbon is C-2, giving $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (2-methylbut-1-ene), which has no geometrical isomers (1 alkene).

(D) $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: loss of H from C-1 gives pent-1-ene, and loss of H from C-3 gives pent-2-ene, which exists as cis and trans forms (3 alkenes).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Find out the major product for the following reaction.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Protonation of the OH group and loss of water give a secondary carbocation on the side-chain carbon $\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}^{+}$, which is attached to the quaternary ring carbon carrying a methyl group.

A C–C bond of the cyclopentane ring migrates to this cationic carbon (ring expansion). The strained five-membered ring becomes a six-membered ring, and the positive charge moves to the former quaternary carbon, which is now a tertiary carbocation bearing a methyl group; the adjacent ring carbon bears the other methyl group.


[IMG]

Loss of a proton from the adjacent $\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})$ carbon gives the most substituted, tetrasubstituted alkene (Saytzeff rule), 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene. Loss of a proton from a ring $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ would give only a trisubstituted alkene, and a methyl shift instead of ring expansion would keep the strained five-membered ring.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
At 298 K

$\mathrm{N}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{NH}_{3}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{K}_{1}=4\times 10^{5}$

$\mathrm{N}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{K}_{2}=1.6\times 10^{12}$

$\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{K}_{3}=1.0\times 10^{-13}$

Based on above equilibria, then equilibrium constant of the reaction, $2\mathrm{NH}_{3}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{5}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$ is $____________$ $\times 10^{-33}$ (Nearest integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

$2\mathrm{NH}_{3}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{5}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$

Clearly, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{k}_{1}}\times \mathrm{k}_{2}\times \mathrm{k}_{3}^{3}$

$=\frac{1.6\times 10^{12}\times 10^{-39}}{4\times 10^{5}}$

$=0.4\times 10^{-32}$

$=4\times 10^{-33}$

text: The denticity of the ligand present in the Fehling's reagent is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fehling's reagent is made by mixing Fehling's solution A (aqueous $\mathrm{CuSO}{}_{4}$) with Fehling's solution B (alkaline sodium potassium tartrate); $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is held in solution as a tartrate complex.

The tartrate ion, $\mathrm{C}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}{}^{2-}$, is ${}^{-}\text{OOC-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-COO}^{-}$; it carries four donor oxygen atoms, one from each carboxylate group and one from each hydroxyl group, so it is a tetradentate ligand.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Total number of acidic oxides among

$\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3},\mathrm{NO}_{2},\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O},\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7},\mathrm{SO}_{2},\mathrm{CO},\mathrm{CaO},\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{NO}$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acidic oxides are non-metal oxides that give acids with water and react with bases:

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$

$2~\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}$

$\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{HClO}{}_{4}$

$\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{CO}$ and $\mathrm{NO}$ are neutral oxides (they react with neither acids nor bases), and $\mathrm{CaO}$ and $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ are basic oxides.

The acidic oxides are $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$ and $\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$, i.e. 4.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift
